findings.title: Bars live in a DuelState module, but every gate that must read them takes only TacticalState and indexes by rooms
findings.claim: §2 says ship 0's laserOffline, canLaunch, flight, laser charge, magazine and shields read the tables by bars, and §7 puts the bars in a new DuelState module `power`. Every function that must change takes a TacticalState and reads `systems[i].rooms[...]`: canLaunch, laserOffline, tickWeapons' chargeRate and shield rate, flyShip through physics, and predictFlight. The spec doesn't say how ship 0's bars reach the tactical state: a field on systems[0], an argument to stepDuel or ShipInput, or a copy each tick. It also leaves out predictFlight. That function runs flyShip with the damage level, and the sim's scripted pilot uses it through predictPath, so the Helm's predicted path and the bot would fly with the wrong engine factor. Tactical commands are admitted in step 1 (canLaunch(d.tactical, 0)), before the power commands in step 2, and the spec never says which bars that admission reads.
findings.evidence: spec L63-L67, L205-L206, L212-L217. weapons.ts:L51 (canLaunch reads rooms[Weapons] < 2), L61 (laserOffline), L154-L155 (chargeRate[rooms[Weapons]]), L159 (shields.rate[rooms[Shields]]). physics.ts:L63 (flyShip(..., rooms[Room.Engines], ...)). predict.ts:L31-L34 (engines = rooms[Engines], fed to flyShip). duel/scripted.ts:L87 (predictPath, used by the sim's scripted pilot). duel/step.ts:L200 (canLaunch admission before any new power phase), L268 (stepDuel(d.tactical, crew): no DuelState).
findings.why: Where the bars live decides the snapshot and hash layout, and the duelModules test has to cover it. One build might store bars on TacticalState.systems[0] and leave the `power` module half-empty. Another might pass bars through ShipInput. Their goldens would differ, and so would their behaviour when a missileLaunch and a Weapons −1 arrive in the same tick. A prediction or scripted pilot left on rooms would quietly desync from the flown path.
findings.fix: Say exactly how ship 0's effective bars reach the tactical code. For example, the tactical system state gains `bars: number[5]`, which the duel writes from `power` before step 1, or stepDuel gains a bars argument. Then list every reader that switches to bars: canLaunch, laserOffline, tickWeapons charge and shields, flyShip in physics, predictFlight/predictPath, and the scan rate. Say that step-1 admission reads the bars as they stood at the start of the tick.

findings.title: The capacity update runs before fire damage, contradicting 'excess bars return at once'
findings.claim: §2 says that when capacity falls (damage rises or the system fails), the excess bars return at once. §7 runs the capacity update at step 8, but firePhase's damage cadence, which also raises a tactical Room, comes later at step 10. A fire-damage rise therefore leaves powered bars above capacity until the next tick's step 8. Meanwhile, the next tick's step-1 admission (canLaunch) runs against those over-capacity bars, and so would stepDuel if the update didn't run first. The spec doesn't say whether repair (step 3) or the overheat at step 11 triggers the same update.
findings.evidence: spec L58-L60 ('the excess bars return to the reactor pool at once'), L218-L221 (8 capacity update, then 10 firePhase damage cadence). duel/fire.ts:L51 (the damage cadence does rooms[p.tacticalRoom]++). spec L107 (overheat returns bars, at step 11).
findings.why: Two implementers would either enforce capacity wherever damage changes or only at step 8. Those give different bars for one tick, and different missile admission on the next tick. The goldens diverge on any seed where a fire's damage tick lands.
findings.fix: Define capacity enforcement as a function, `clampToCapacity`, called right after every change to damage or failure: after stepDuel (step 6/7), after the firePhase damage cadence (step 10) and at overheat (step 11). Alternatively, move the single capacity update to after step 10 and state that overheat clamps inline.

findings.title: The scan rate per Sensors bar is fixed when the scan starts; the spec doesn't say when the table is read or what 0 bars does to a scan
findings.claim: The rate table gives Science and Helm/Weapons scan rates per Sensors bar, with 0 at 0 bars. scanCommand stores the rate in t.scan.rate when the command is applied, so a later Sensors change doesn't touch a scan already running. At 0 bars, a contactScan would start a scan at rate 0 that never progresses, with result 'applied'. The spec doesn't say whether a bar change updates a running scan, or whether a scan at 0 bars is rejected (`unavailable`) or paused.
findings.evidence: spec L81-L82 (scan rows), L63-L64. tactical/science.ts:L12-L20 (s.rate set once; same-level re-scan is noop unless the rate is higher). duel/step.ts:L248 (rate chosen at admission from SCAN_RATE_SCIENCE/OTHER).
findings.why: Two builds would split here: one rereads the rate every tick, the other freezes it. That changes scan times whenever Engineering moves Sensors bars, which is exactly the trade-off the spike is meant to test.
findings.fix: State that the scan's per-tick progress reads the table at the current Sensors bars every tick, so s.rate becomes the station's base or is recomputed each tick. Also state that a contactScan with Sensors at 0 bars is rejected `unavailable`, or that it starts and pauses. Pick one.

findings.title: Fires in non-point rooms, spread ignitions and breaches have no event shape
findings.claim: Today's fireWork, fireOut and fireStart events carry `room` as a tactical Room index (0..2). §4 adds firefighting in B, Q, M, L and H, fire spread through fireStep, breach rolls and patching. None of these has a tactical Room, and the spec defines no events for them. The HUD's breach and fire icons and any cues need to know which room changed.
findings.evidence: spec L143-L153. duel/step.ts:L76 and L81 (events keyed by point.tacticalRoom). duel/fire.ts:L38 (fireStart room: e.room, a tactical Room). hazards/fire.ts:L35-L36 (spread ignition pushes no event).
findings.why: Implementers would each invent different event kinds and fields, or emit none. Events are part of the step's output that tests and the app read.
findings.fix: Add events keyed by interior room index, for example fireWork, fireOut and fireStart with `interiorRoom`, plus breachStart, breachWork and breachPatched. Say whether spread and overheat ignitions push fireStart. Or state that the HUD reads state only and these rooms push no events.

findings.title: The overheat draw's consumption when the room is already burning, and the order across systems, are unstated
findings.claim: §3 says 'One rng.hazards draw at OVERHEAT_FIRE_CHANCE ignites its room if that room isn't burning'. That reads two ways: skip the draw when the room is burning, or always draw, which is what heat.ts does ('draw always consumed'). It also doesn't say in what order several systems overheating on the same hazard tick draw. Weapons and Sensors share room O.
findings.evidence: spec L107-L108, L226. heat.ts:L40 (draw always consumed; no-op if burning), L46 (ascending index).
findings.why: Either reading changes the rng.hazards stream, and so the goldens.
findings.fix: Say 'the draw is always consumed, in ascending system index (Shields, Weapons, Engines, Sensors)'.

prior.note: §7 now gives a numbered order and the hazard cadence (tick − baseTick) % HAZARD_EVERY, which is correct. But steps 9 and 10 put the hit fire/breach rolls before firePhase's damage cadence, while today's firePhase applies the damage cadence first and then igniteFromHits (duel/fire.ts:L45-L54; duel/step.ts:L270). So 'the rest is today's order' (spec L210) is false. A room ignited on a cadence tick would be damaged at once under the spec's order and not under today's. Either restore today's order (10 before 9) or state the change. The capacity-timing problem in the same list is raised as a new finding.
